item.title: Renting on the Island of Ireland
item.description:
This research, commissioned by Threshold and Housing Rights, examines the lived reality of renting across the island of Ireland, aiming to equip decision-makers, advocates and practitioners with robust evidence to support effective action.

By combining statistical findings with qualitative testimonies, the research reveals a lived experience of renters, grounded in data and hard evidence.

We conducted two large representative public opinion polls of renters in the private rental sector. One of those was in the Republic of Ireland (ROI), and the other was in Northern Ireland (NI), combined with in-depth qualitative interviews to produce a comparative study of renting in ROI and NI.

item.title: Of The Small Amount Listening, Not Enough Were Persuaded.
item.description:
Around four in ten voters (41%) did not watch the final televised debate of the presidential election, which aired during Prime Time’s 9:35pm slot on RTÉ One last Tuesday. According to 40% of voters, Catherine Connolly enjoyed the best performance, compared to 11% for Humphreys and 9% who were unsure.

Strikingly, every intended Connolly voter that watched the just over hour-long showdown said that she won the debate. Connolly supporters were also the most engaged overall – reporting the highest rates of viewership among all other voting groups. This kind of unwavering and disciplined engagement points to a higher propensity among this group to have turned out on polling day.

item.title: Estimation Error in Portfolio Optimisation
item.description:
Abstract

This project evaluates four portfolio optimization methods—ranging from classical mean-variance to Wasserstein robust CVaR—against an equal-weighted benchmark using a rolling 60-month out-of-sample backtest across 12 US industry portfolios. It investigates whether progressively mitigating parameter estimation noise and tail risk translates into genuine out-of-sample performance gains after accounting for trading costs.

item.title: Statistical Evaluation of Cross-Sectional Equity Trading Signals
item.description:
Abstract

This project evaluates 54 cross-sectional equity trading signals across seven factor families to determine whether multiple testing corrections, factor residualization, and signal blending improve out-of-sample portfolio stability over selecting top historical winners. Tested on a locked out-of-sample period with linear transaction costs, it demonstrates how backtest overfitting and signal collinearity erode unadjusted alpha, emphasizing the need for rigorous statistical screening in quantitative strategy construction.
